name: f_divergence_convexity_sweep_classical
divergence_log: Classical f-divergences D_f(p||q) = sum q f(p/q) are defined on a commuting simplex and obey joint convexity and DPI for any convex f with f(1)=0. Quantum f-divergences require operator-convex f (Petz) and tr(sigma^{1/2} f(sigma^{-1/2} rho sigma^{-1/2}) sigma^{1/2}); not every classical convex f lifts monotonically to the quantum setting. The classical substrate cannot detect the operator-monotonicity gap that separates Petz-admissible f from generic convex f in the noncommuting regime.
